title: Verifier‑Assisted versus LLM‑Only Pre‑deployment Network‑Change Validation: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We measured whether integrating a deterministic pre‑deployment verifier plus a bounded automated repair budget increases the fraction of intent‑driven network‑change proposals that pass semantic validation compared with accepting a single LLM candidate. In a preregistered paired design (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) we executed 300 paired intents (100 per difficulty stratum: low/medium/high) using gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5. For each intent a single shared_initial candidate was generated and evaluated under two conditions: baseline (accept single shot) and guarded (deterministic validation and ≤1 automated repair). Outcomes: baseline 299/300 unflagged passes (0.9966667), guarded 300/300 (1.0); contingency n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; absolute paired difference = 0.0033333; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% paired bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.01] (bootstrap_seed = 1729, B = 10000). Under the supplied synthetic suite and repair budget the single‑shot generator was near ceiling, limiting observable deterministic rescue. We archive preregistration, execution, and analysis artifacts and interpret results with respect to estimand conditioning, validator coverage, repair budget, and operational deployment policies.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to NetOps tasks such as intent→configuration translation, configuration synthesis, and automated repair. For pre‑deployment network changes, semantic correctness properties—ordering/sequence constraints, reachability, and policy preservation—are operationally critical and are not guaranteed by syntactic well‑formedness alone. A pragmatic engineering pattern is a generate→validate→repair scaffold that pairs a generative model with a deterministic verifier and bounded automated repair. However, the measurable benefit of such guarded pipelines depends strongly on the experimental estimand (what is held fixed), the generator single‑shot quality, the validator's expressiveness, and permitted repair budget.

This paper reports a preregistered, artifact‑archived paired experiment (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) that isolates the deterministic rescue provided by a verifier plus a single constrained repair when the same single LLM draw is reused across conditions (the shared_initial estimand). The central research question is: does adding a deterministic verifier and at most one automated repair increase the probability that a single LLM candidate passes semantic pre‑deployment validation compared with accepting that same candidate without repair? Our contributions are (1) a preregistered paired evaluation that conditions on a single shared_initial LLM output per intent, (2) a complete execution and analysis bundle with validator traces and the single automated repair transcript archived, and (3) an evidence‑grounded interpretation of estimand conditioning, ceiling effects, and operational implications for NetOps CI/CD policies.
sections.related_work:
Prior work documents active application of LLMs to NetOps tasks (intent translation, template synthesis, protocol test generation, repair) and the emergence of tool‑augmented agentic frameworks that call external validators and simulators to coordinate multi‑step workflows [1–6]. Several system papers and surveys emphasize generate→validate→repair scaffolds and planner‑centric or ReAct‑style tool augmentation to reduce hallucinations and enforce semantic constraints [4,7]. Empirical reports show that deterministic checks and validation scaffolds can improve correctness metrics relative to unconstrained generation, but reported magnitudes vary with validator coverage, task distribution, and whether evaluations permit resampling or verifier‑guided regeneration [3,5].

Two methodological themes motivate the present design. First, many prior evaluations conflate deterministic validation with benefits arising from additional model draws or interactive regeneration, making it difficult to isolate the purely post‑generation deterministic rescue attributable to a verifier and bounded repair [3]. Second, existing NetOps benchmarks often emphasize syntactic/template correctness rather than semantically rich invariants (sequence constraints, reachability, policy preservation), which limits operational generality of evaluation claims; proposals for verifier‑centric benchmarks advocate richer semantic checks but community adoption is incomplete [2,8]. Our study explicitly conditions on a single LLM draw and a small repair budget to bound the deterministic rescue that such a guarded pipeline can provide under limited model‑call budgets.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered (cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) and archived prior to the main run. The primary estimand is the absolute paired difference in unflagged verifier‑pass proportion (guarded − baseline) computed on N = 300 paired intents after the prespecified inclusion/exclusion rules. The confirmatory analysis executor and inference procedures (paired contingency reporting, exact two‑sided McNemar, paired bootstrap CI) were fixed before observing main‑run outcomes; preregistration SHA‑256 = 425cb1652354120cf48f686b964723d64c76d0a8abe53cd5b5ad0eaa1af71fc7.

Task suite and stratification. Tasks were generated deterministically into a synthetic_topology_suite and stratified by difficulty metadata into three strata (low/medium/high) using changes per intent and dependency counts; the confirmatory run sampled 100 paired intents per stratum (300 pairs total). Each task manifest encodes the natural‑language intent, initial and expected final states, sequencing constraints (e.g., must_be_down_for_fields), preservation invariants, and protected interfaces. The deterministic task generator and manifest format are archived with the run bundle.

Shared_initial protocol and model configuration. To isolate deterministic validator/repair rescue from generator resampling effects we implemented a shared_initial protocol: for each pair the pipeline produced exactly one shared_initial candidate using the declared generator (gpt-5-mini) and reused that identical candidate for both baseline and guarded conditions. Reuse prevents differences due to independent additional model draws and measures only deterministic validation and bounded repair applied to the identical output. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (execution manifest records requested_model = "gpt-5-mini").

Deterministic validator and bounded repair. Semantic evaluation used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implementing the preregistered full_intent_constraint_validation rule. The validator deterministically checks sequencing invariants, required command counts, preservation of unspecified state, topology reachability invariants encoded by the synthetic suite, and forbidden‑template protections. Scoring is binary: an unflagged candidate is a pass. The guarded pipeline permits at most one automated repair attempt per pair (repair budget ≤ 1). The repair operator is a constrained edit routine limited to localized sequencing insertions and small edits; it is applied only when the validator flags the shared_initial candidate and the repaired candidate is re‑validated deterministically. Repair candidates that remain flagged after the permitted edit count are counted as failures for the guarded condition.

Execution accounting and contamination controls. The run used the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter in scientific_confirmatory mode. The preregistration included deterministic contamination detection (negative controls and reachability invariant checks) and explicit exclusion/missingness rules: pairs are excluded only if both pipeline calls fail due to provider/infrastructure outages; single‑call failures are handled per the executor's complete_pair_primary policy with preplanned sensitivity analyses. The execution manifest, provider audit counts, and deterministic reconciliation are archived with the run bundle to enable verification of shared_initial reuse and accounting integrity.

Analysis plan. The preregistered confirmatory analysis computes contingency counts (n11,n10,n01,n00), the absolute paired difference, an exact two‑sided McNemar test on discordant counts, and a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (seed = 1729, B = 10000). The primary test is the single pre‑registered hypothesis H1 on the main N = 300 pairs. Secondary and stratum tests are exploratory and subject to multiplicity control if reported.
sections.results:
Execution integrity. The adapter completed the confirmatory run with planned_episode_count = 600 and completed_episode_count = 600, yielding complete_pair_count = 300 paired observations under the shared_initial protocol. Provider/audit records show hosted_model_call_event_count = 301 (300 shared_initial generations plus one repair invocation) and stage_counts indicating shared_initial_generation = 300 and repair = 1. Deterministic reconciliation confirmed consistent episode accounting and reported all_deterministic_consistency_checks_passed = true. No pairs were excluded under the preregistered rules.

Primary confirmatory outcomes. Binary scoring produced baseline_success_count = 299 and guarded_success_count = 300 (baseline = 299/300 = 0.9966667; guarded = 300/300 = 1.0). The paired contingency table is n11 = 299, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The exact two‑sided McNemar test returned p = 1.0. The absolute paired improvement (guarded − baseline) equals 0.0033333. The paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI computed with seed = 1729 and B = 10000 is [0.00, 0.01]. Because discordance is minimal (m = n10 + n01 = 1), the exact test has limited sensitivity and the bootstrap CI bounds the plausible absolute improvement to at most one percentage point in this experimental context.

Per‑stratum diagnostics and repair trace. Per‑stratum tallies were: low baseline = 100/100 and guarded = 100/100; medium baseline = 100/100 and guarded = 100/100; high baseline = 99/100 and guarded = 100/100. The single discordant pair occurred in the high difficulty stratum. The solitary repair invocation corrected a sequencing omission (missing required 'admin down' before a VLAN/MTU change) via one constrained insertion; after the edit the deterministic validator reported valid == true for the corrected candidate. The repair therefore produced a deterministic rescue for that episode under the preregistered bounded edit operator.

Contamination and missingness. Contamination checks flagged no unexpected negative‑control passes. The missingness summary reports no failed or unscorable episodes and no excluded pairs under preregistered rules. The low marginal repair usage (repair_stage_count = 1) indicates minimal additional model‑call cost for deterministic rescue under the chosen repair budget and edit‑operator design.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation with respect to estimand conditioning. Conditioning on a single LLM draw per intent (shared_initial) corresponds to operational policies that tightly constrain model calls for cost, latency, or governance reasons. Under that policy the guarded pipeline measures only deterministic validator and bounded repair rescue applied to the same candidate. Workflows that permit resampling, verifier‑guided generation, or interactive steering change the estimand and typically increase achievable success rates by exploiting generator variance; such workflows must be evaluated under a different preregistered estimand.

Ceiling effects and power implications. The preregistration targeted detection of a 10 percentage‑point absolute improvement with planned power ≈0.8 based on an optional pilot to estimate discordance; that pilot was not executed. The observed near‑ceiling baseline (299/300) produced minimal discordance (m = 1) and limited power to detect small absolute differences. This practical outcome highlights the value of small calibration pilots when generator performance may approach ceiling on a chosen suite and the importance of aligning power planning with expected baseline performance.

Validator coverage and failure‑mode dependence. The observed failure mode was a sequencing omission; other classes (reachability violations, forbidden ACL removal) were not observed at scale on this synthetic suite. The marginal utility of a guarded pipeline thus depends on (a) the deployment distribution of failure modes and (b) validator expressiveness: richer validators that detect reachability or policy semantics may increase observed rescue rates. Conversely, if operator policy disallows automated edits, the guarded pipeline's deterministic rescue is operationally limited to detection and human escalation.

Repair budget tradeoffs and operational cost. We intentionally limited automated repair to a single constrained edit to measure bounded deterministic rescue and to bound model‑call cost. Iterative repair, larger edit operators, or interactive verifier‑guided regeneration would increase rescue opportunities but address a different estimand and impose higher model‑call costs. In this run deterministic rescue required only one additional repair call across 300 pairs (model_calls_used = 301), indicating a low marginal cost for the observed rescue under the chosen settings.

Implications for NetOps CI/CD. Organizations must align evaluation estimands with operational choices: if pipelines permit multiple model calls or verifier‑guided regeneration, evaluations should allow resampling and interactive steering. If model calls are tightly budgeted, the shared_initial estimand provides an operationally meaningful bound on deterministic verifier/repair rescue for a single LLM draw. Our artifact archive enables forensic inspection of per‑episode validator traces and repair transcripts to inform repair operator design and validator coverage for production adoption.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered, artifact‑archived paired comparison between a verifier‑assisted pipeline (deterministic validator + ≤1 automated repair) and accepting a single‑shot LLM candidate under the shared_initial estimand on 300 synthetic NetOps intents using gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Baseline single‑shot generation produced 299/300 unflagged verifier passes and the guarded pipeline 300/300, yielding an absolute paired improvement of 0.00333 (exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI [0.00,0.01]). Deterministic validator+repair rescued a single sequencing omission under the bounded repair budget. The near‑ceiling baseline limits inferential sensitivity to small absolute improvements under the shared_initial estimand. We release full preregistration, execution, and analysis artifacts to support reproducibility and targeted follow‑up studies that vary estimand conditioning, model strength, task distribution, or repair budget.

limitations: Synthetic benchmark: tasks and topologies were generated by the preregistered deterministic task generator and may not reflect all real‑world heterogeneity; different failure‑mode distributions could change guarded pipeline utility.
Single model and validator: only gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 were evaluated; results may not generalize to other LLMs or to validators with different semantic coverage.

Ceiling effect: baseline single‑shot performance was near 100% on this suite (299/300), producing minimal discordance and reduced power to detect small absolute improvements relative to larger pre‑specified targets.
Pilot not executed: the preregistered pilot intended for discordance estimation and power calibration was not run; no post‑preregistration power recalculation was performed.

Estimand conditioning: the shared_initial protocol conditions the estimand on a single LLM candidate and therefore does not measure verifier benefit that would arise from allowing independent alternative LLM candidates per condition (resampling or iterative generation).
Repair budget: the guarded condition permitted at most one automated repair per pair; larger or iterative repair strategies could yield different outcomes and higher model‑call costs.
